previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for observation following an ERCP performed to evaluate recurrent acute pancreatitis. The procedure showed no biliary abnormalities but confirmed chronic pancreatitis with a mildly dilated, irregular pancreatic duct. A temporary stent was placed to prevent post-procedural pancreatitis. The patient reported persistent abdominal pain and anxiety post-procedure, initially refusing full cooperation. Labs remained stable without evidence of acute pancreatitis, and she tolerated oral intake. Her diabetes was managed with Lantus and Humalog, and her anxiety was addressed with continued diazepam. She was discharged home in stable condition with plans to return in two weeks for stent removal.
